claims.text: Where do I send a publisher who has never read anything on newsroom.sgit.ai?
claims.quote: Where do I send a publisher who has never read anything on newsroom.sgit.ai?

claims.text: The publishers page is a good distillation but was written once, and the site, still in its explorer phase, changes most days.
claims.quote: But it was written once, and this site does not stand still.

claims.text: Sections a reader has already read now fold away, with a bar to choose how; it shipped on 17 October with the change that made the meter charge for what is read, and nothing on the publishers page says so.
claims.quote: it shipped on 17 October with the change that made the meter charge for what is read

claims.text: A section sits between the desks and the personas: the newsroom as one audience reads it, with start here, latest, the features they can use, every relevant article in streams, and how it stays current.
claims.quote: A section sits between the two: the newsroom as one audience reads it

claims.text: The first section is for publishers, second in the Newsroom menu at the top of every page.
claims.quote: The first is for publishers, second in the Newsroom menu at the top of every page.

claims.text: Start here is five pieces chosen by the editor, each with a sentence saying why: the founding argument, the arithmetic of one article, the meter, why agents will pay to read, and quality control when agents write.
claims.quote: Five pieces, chosen by me, each with a sentence saying why

value.unit: pieces to start with, chosen by hand

claims.text: Nothing on the page is listed by hand except the five to start with; the rest comes from the desk and controlled subjects every article is given at publication, which run on every release.
claims.quote: Nothing on the page is listed by hand except the five to start with.

claims.text: A section is one small file of rules in plain JSON written against that data; streams are tried in order and an article goes in the first one it matches.
claims.quote: Streams are tried in order and an article goes in the first one it matches.

claims.text: The stream how news gets paid for is anything with the subjects micropayments, story vaults or local news, or anything on the news desk about the agent-readable web, journalism or pricing that is not a reply.
claims.quote: anything with the subjects micropayments, story vaults or local news

claims.text: Features come from a new register, one entry per feature with what it does, when it shipped, its status and where to try it, added in the release that ships it.
claims.quote: A feature is added in the release that ships it.

claims.text: An article about paying for news is in the publishers' section the day it is published, in the right stream, saying why; the section is maintained by the same rules that maintain everything else.
claims.quote: The section is not written; it is maintained by the same rules that maintain everything else.

claims.text: The first run placed 79 articles; after the fixes, 69, and each wrong placement was a lesson about the classification rather than the section.
claims.quote: The first run placed 79 articles; after the fixes below, 69.

value.unit: articles placed after the fixes, against the first run

claims.text: Three talks from the Portugal history series landed under how news gets paid for because the controlled subject journalism absorbs the raw tag history; the section now excludes them with the reason written beside each.
claims.quote: because the controlled subject journalism absorbs the raw tag history

claims.text: The subject the agent-readable web had swept up an article on dark mode and one on a tokens hook; the stream now takes it only from articles whose first desk is news, with two named exceptions.
claims.quote: had swept up an article on dark mode and one on a tokens hook

claims.text: Answers to FT Strategies and to Reader Skills went to how news gets paid for because they are tagged story vault; the answers stream is now tried first.
claims.quote: the answers stream is now tried first

claims.text: The lesson is the one of search as navigation: the better the taxonomy, the less anyone curates by hand, and every fix is a rule with a reason in a file anyone can read.
claims.quote: the better the taxonomy, the less anyone has to curate by hand

claims.text: Sections for security leads and boards, people building with agents, and founders and investors can follow the same pattern: one more file of rules and five pieces to start with.
claims.quote: Each is one more file of rules and five pieces to start with; the features and the placement come for free.

claims.text: Each section has a machine-readable twin, so an agent sent to the newsroom on a publisher's behalf can read it as easily as the publisher can.
claims.quote: an agent sent to the newsroom on a publisher's behalf can read the section as easily as the publisher can

claims.text: The start here list is the editor's and will go stale unless he changes it; everything else updates itself.
claims.quote: The start here list is mine, and will go stale

claims.text: The placement is only as good as the classification; three exclusions and two exceptions are written into the rules today.
claims.quote: The placement is only as good as the classification.

claims.text: The features register starts today, and some features have no shipping date in it because none could be confirmed from the release notes.
claims.quote: The features register starts today.

claims.text: One section exists; the others are a proposal.
claims.quote: One section exists. The others are a proposal.

claims.text: The publishers page itself is unchanged; it is imported from sgit.ai and the section links to it as the overview.
claims.quote: The publishers page itself is unchanged.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 18 October 2026; the rules, the data, the features register and the build code are published, and the site's agent wrote it up.
claims.quote: A voice memo from me on 18 October 2026.
